name: Gdańsk
title: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement Gdańsk | Tankers & Docks
description: Ship thickness measurement in Gdańsk for crude tankers at Naftoport, container ships and repair-yard dockings: CAP, ESP and renewal survey UTM of hulls.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement and Hull Gauging in Gdańsk
intro: Gdańsk is Poland's largest port, with ocean-going container ships at Baltic Hub, crude tankers at Naftoport, bulk carriers in the Northern Port and large-scale ship repair at Remontowa. Inspection demand runs from CAP gauging on tankers to renewal-survey steel lists in dock and scrubber piping on container ships. We mobilise a team from India to Gdańsk for each job, scheduled against the docking slot, the discharge programme or the ship's call.

highlights.p: Naftoport in the Northern Port receives crude tankers supplying Polish refineries. CAP and vetting-driven gauging on these ships has to be fitted around discharge, ballasting and the time needed for gas-freeing.

Remontowa Ship Repair Yard docks ferries, tankers, offshore and cargo ships in its floating docks. Readings taken in the first days in dock tell the yard how much steel to plan for before its work schedule is fixed.

Baltic Hub takes large container ships on direct services from Asia as well as Baltic feeders. Scrubber wash-water and overboard piping on these ships is a frequent gauging scope during their port stays.

port.h: Port of Gdańsk: Northern Port, Inner Port and the ships they handle
p: The Port of Gdańsk is split into two very different parts. The Northern Port, built out into the Gulf of Gdańsk, is the deep-water side: the Baltic Hub container terminal, the Naftoport crude and product terminal, and terminals for coal, other dry bulk and liquid cargoes. The Inner Port follows the Martwa Wisła and the port canal back towards the city, with quays for general cargo, ro-ro, grain and other bulk, and the ferry terminal for the service to Nynäshamn in Sweden. Between them they make Gdańsk Poland's largest port and one of the main gateways to Central Europe.

The fleet is correspondingly broad. Baltic Hub handles ocean-going container ships on direct services from Asia alongside Baltic feeders. Naftoport receives crude tankers carrying seaborne supply for Polish refineries, and product tankers work cargo at the liquid berths. Bulk carriers work coal, grain and other dry cargo in the Northern Port and along the inner quays, and ro-ro, general cargo and ro-pax ships fill out the Inner Port. Gdańsk is also a ship-repair centre: Remontowa Ship Repair Yard docks merchant ships of many types, and the city's shipbuilding tradition continues in newbuilding and steel fabrication yards.

Each trade gives a different window for gauging. Crude tankers spend time discharging and ballasting, and some wait in the Gulf of Gdańsk before berthing. Bulk carriers load or discharge over days. Container ships have scheduled calls that are short but predictable, which suits prepared, tightly scoped work such as scrubber piping. Ships docking at Remontowa have a fixed period with full access. What sets Gdańsk apart is the concentration of tanker vetting and docking work in one place. A tanker past fifteen years may need CAP gauging, and a docking at Remontowa may follow, so the gauging done at Naftoport and the readings taken in dock should be planned as one programme rather than two separate jobs.

facilities.h: Where we gauge ships in Gdańsk
p: In the Northern Port, terminal rules shape the work. At Naftoport, nothing happens on a tanker without a permit from both ship and terminal; within that, the deck and pipelines are measured during discharge, while cargo tank internals need gas-free certification and therefore dedicated time alongside, at anchor or in a yard. At Baltic Hub, container ship calls are short, so scopes are agreed with the chief engineer in advance and concentrate on what can be reached in the time, typically scrubber piping, deck structure and accessible tanks. CAP thickness measurement on a tanker is the opposite case: a large, structured scope that needs days rather than hours.

When a ship enters one of Remontowa's floating docks, preparing access is the yard's job; measuring the shell, double bottom, tanks and piping as each is handed over is ours. The aim is to give the yard and the class surveyor a renewal list within the first days of the stay. Along the Inner Port quays, bulk, general cargo and ro-ro ships are gauged during cargo operations. Ships riding at anchor in the Gulf of Gdańsk are boarded by launch, which the agent books, and that is often where pre-purchase and pre-docking gauging is done.
list: Naftoport, Northern Port — crude tankers; main deck, pipelines and, once gas-free, cargo and ballast tank structure when the discharge programme allows
Baltic Hub container terminal — ocean-going and feeder container ships; scrubber piping, deck and ballast-tank gauging during calls
Northern Port bulk terminals — coal, grain and other dry bulk; bulk carriers measured in holds, hoppers and on tank tops between loading stages
Remontowa Ship Repair Yard — floating docks taking ferries, tankers and offshore units; survey gauging that sets the steel list early in the stay
Inner Port quays on the Martwa Wisła — general cargo, ro-ro and ferry berths; vehicle-deck and hold gauging during port stays
Gulf of Gdańsk anchorage — tankers and bulk carriers held before berthing at the Northern Port; the team goes out by a launch booked through the agent

context.h: Polish regulation and market context in Gdańsk
p: Port state control in Gdańsk is carried out under the Paris MoU, and ships in the Gulf of Gdańsk must burn fuel at or below 0.10% sulphur, the Baltic ECA limit, unless they clean their exhaust. Large container ships arriving from Asia are among the ships most likely to carry exhaust gas scrubbers, and the acidic wash-water they handle attacks discharge piping and the shell connection, which is why owners order regular gauging of those lines. Under the EU ETS for shipping, from 2024, voyages arriving from outside the EU are partly covered and voyages between EU ports fully, and FuelEU Maritime applies from 2025, so the steel renewal decision on an older ship docking here is weighed against a growing set of regulatory obligations.

The tanker trade brings vetting to the fore. Oil-major vetting through SIRE inspections, and CAP, which charterers commonly request for tankers over about fifteen years, both rest on the condition of hull structure, and the IACS ESP rules, UR Z10.1 and Z10.4 for oil tankers, require gauging that grows with each renewal survey. Gdańsk is also where the Polish Register of Shipping has its headquarters. Every society applies the same IACS rule, UR Z17: the firm measuring thickness for a class survey needs the approval of that ship's own society.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Gdańsk
jobs.p: Gdańsk work centres on tankers, container ships and dockings, with bulk carriers and the ro-pax trade adding steady demand. Many jobs link a port call with a later docking, so the scope is planned as a programme. Crude tanker gauging in particular is split between what can be done during discharge and what needs gas-free days or the yard. A ship inspection in Gdańsk is therefore scoped with the charterer's timetable in view.
list: CAP gauging of cargo and ballast tanks on a crude tanker after discharge at Naftoport, in a gas-free window negotiated with the charterer before she sails
Renewal-survey gauging on a ro-pax in a Remontowa floating dock, with first-day readings on bottom plating, ballast tanks and vehicle decks
Scrubber wash-water, overboard discharge and sea water piping on an ocean-going container ship at Baltic Hub, measured inside the engine casing during her call
ESP intermediate-survey gauging on a bulk carrier loading in the Northern Port, in holds not yet loaded and in gas-freed topside tanks
Pre-purchase gauging of a product tanker at the Gulf of Gdańsk anchorage, reporting deck, piping and ballast-tank condition to the buyer

logistics: The team flies into Gdańsk Lech Wałęsa Airport, which serves the whole Tricity area, and reaches the Northern Port, the Inner Port or the shipyard by road. The ship's agent applies for ISPS passes at Naftoport, Baltic Hub and the bulk terminals and books a launch for ships at anchor, while the shipyard handles entry for dockings. Poland is a Schengen state, so our technicians travelling from India hold a Schengen visa; we lock in dates once the docking slot or discharge programme is known.

faqs.q: Can you carry out CAP gauging on a crude tanker at Naftoport?
faqs.a: Partly, and fully if the ship can stay gas-free long enough. A CAP survey reads a great deal of tank structure, and that requires the tanks gas-free, ventilated and safely accessible, which a normal discharge call does not provide. During discharge we can cover the main deck and pipelines; the tank programme needs gas-free days alongside or at anchor, which the charterer and terminal must accept, or else a yard stay. We plan the split with the superintendent before the ship arrives.

faqs.q: Why do container ships need scrubber piping gauged?
faqs.a: Scrubber wash-water is acidic, and it thins steel discharge piping, distance pieces and the area around the overboard connection from the inside. A leak there sits close to the ship's side, which is why owners measure these lines at regular intervals. On a container ship at Baltic Hub we gauge the accessible runs inside the engine casing and scrubber spaces during the call, and report wall loss against the original thickness.

faqs.q: Does the Polish Register of Shipping's presence in Gdańsk change the gauging rules?
faqs.a: No. Under UR Z17, which binds every IACS society alike, gauging that feeds a class survey has to come from a firm the ship's own society has approved, and the class surveyor attends and verifies the readings. Gauging done for an owner's own planning, a purchase or a vetting inspection follows the owner's requirements, so it is worth stating the purpose of the readings when the job is ordered.

faqs.q: How do you plan gauging for a docking at Remontowa?
faqs.a: Ideally in two steps. A pre-docking gauging at an earlier port call identifies likely renewal areas so the yard can order steel. In dock, we start on the shell and the tanks with the most expected wastage as soon as staging and cleaning are done, and hand readings to the yard and the surveyor daily, so renewal areas are marked while the yard's work plan is still open.
